core.title: Name every produced or consumed artifact theme-first
core.given: A produced or consumed artifact/contract identity exists (new, renamed or pre-existing)
core.when: Identities are validated at the CONFIRM phase
core.then: The identity must be theme-first: it parses as {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? — at least one separator is required (theme plus aspect), categories are repeatable, the variant is optional and dot-separated — every colon- or dot-separated token is lowercase kebab-case, and the leading theme is declared in the canonical theme map.
prefer: Start the identity with a theme declared in the canonical theme map, then optional categories, then the aspect, then an optional .variant
Use lowercase kebab-case for every token between colons and dots
If no fitting theme exists, declare it in the canonical theme map first rather than inventing it inline
avoid: Using a leading theme that is not declared in the canonical theme map
Names without a theme:aspect colon structure, such as dot-only names with no theme segment
core.why: Artifact identities are the join keys between producers and consumers and contract paths mirror them; a fixed theme-first grammar anchored to a canonical theme map keeps them parseable, unambiguous and consistently located.
evidence: The artifact-identity naming check reports no finding for any produced or consumed artifact at the CONFIRM phase (confirm-blocking)
On failure, the finding names the offending artifact name and the reason
verification: Checked at the CONFIRM phase with confirm-blocking enforcement; disposition strict, severity 3
Applies to every produced or consumed artifact/contract identity — new, renamed or pre-existing — not only changed ones; no path or change gate is implied

The check covers grammar parsing, token casing, and theme declaration against the canonical theme map; the validator family/template/variant and finding ids are realization details named by each stack's own check

fires: At CONFIRM, a produced or consumed artifact identity does not parse under the theme-first grammar
At CONFIRM, an artifact identity's leading theme is not declared in the canonical theme map
At CONFIRM, a contract identity uses uppercase or non-kebab tokens
At CONFIRM, an existing, unchanged artifact identity is dot-only with no theme segment
doesNotFire: Every produced and consumed artifact/contract identity parses under the grammar, uses kebab-case tokens, and starts with a theme declared in the canonical theme map
The name being checked is not a produced or consumed artifact/contract identity

profileRequirements.meaning: Path of the canonical theme map: the registry in which the leading theme of every produced or consumed artifact/contract identity must be declared

proposedKeys.meaning: Path of the canonical theme map: the registry that declares the themes a theme-first artifact/contract identity may start with
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group covers per-artifact URN shapes, bindings and declarations, and the layout/roots groups cover plan-artifact placement generally, but no key names the canonical registry that authorizes the leading theme of an artifact identity

neutralityNotes: The theme-first grammar ({theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})?, colon/dot separators, lowercase kebab-case tokens) is kept verbatim in the core: it defines the convention itself and names no stack, runtime, framework or language. The only concrete injected through the profile is the canonical theme-map location (urn.theme_map, proposed — no existing vocabulary key covers a theme registry). CONFIRM is an ATDD process phase, not a stack concept, and stays in the core. Detector/validator/term/finding ids (planner_artifact_theme_first_identity, naming_pattern variant, artifact_theme_first_identity) and the concrete ok/bad example names remain bunOnly: the core's verification describes the check generically and each realization substitutes its own ids; bun.json stays the worked reference example. The core is no weaker and no stronger: the three then-conditions, the all-identities (not only changed) scope, the empty unless, confirm-blocking/strict/severity-3 enforcement and the failure-evidence shape are all preserved.
